newsitem.title: USA: SBC of U.S. closes deal to form Swiss Diax.
newsitem.headline: SBC of U.S. closes deal to form Swiss Diax.

text.p: SBC Commmunications Inc said it completed a previously announced deal to form Diax, a new Swiss telecom venture set up to compete versus the Swiss national Telecom Postal, Telephone and Telegraph company.

SBC said its partner in the joint venture is made of Switzerland's six utilities, which together will own 60 percent of Diax. SBC, the telecommunications operating partner of the venture, will own the remaining 40 percent.
The ownership structure had not been disclosed previously.

The company said additional details of the deal, including the level of investment, managment structure, staffing and board representation, will be annnouced at a press conference in June in Switzerland.
The U.S.-based phone carrier said the Diax venture bolsters its presence in Europe ahead of January 1988, when many markets will be opened up to competition, including Switzerland's.
An SBC spokesman said the structure of deal remains to be approved by the Swiss government's competition commission, a process expected to be completed next month.
He declined comment on further details of the company's structure.

Diax faces competition not only from Swiss Telecom, but also a consortium formed by Swiss Federal Railways SBB, the supermarket chain Migro and Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) that is known as Newtelco AG.
"Diax represents a great blend of expertise that will benefit Swiss consumers and businesses," Edward Whiteacre, SBC's chairman and chief executive, said in a statement.
"No one knows the Swiss marketplace better than our utility company partners, and SBC's capabilities and experience in developing telecommunications companies around the world is unsurpassed."

Diax will be a full-service provider to residential and business customers. It has under construction an advanced digital fiber optic network that will provide all major Swiss cities with rapid, high-quality transmission links nationwide.
SBC said Diax will also bid on Swiss wireless licenses when they become available.

The $10 billlion Swiss telecommunications market is the world's tenth largest, with more telephones per capita than any country other than Sweden. Annual revenue per phone line of US$1,700 is the highest in the world, according to SBC.
Switzerland is the third country in Europe where SBC has telecommunications interests.
A week ago, SBC finalized a deal to form Cegetel in France with French utility Generale des Eaux, British Telecom and Germany's Mannesmann AG.
In 1995, SBC merged its U.K. cable and telephone interests with Telewest Communications Plc, creating the U.K.'s largest cable operator. SBC retains a minority share interest.

SBC's utilty partners in Diax are Aare-Tessin Electricity AG (Atel), BKW FMB Energy AG (BKW), Centralschweizerische Kraftwerke AG (CKW), Elektrizitaetsgesellschaft Laufenberg AG (EGL), L'Energie de l'Ouest-Suisse (EOS) and Northostschweizerische Kraftwerke (NOK).
